mars_base.label: Mars base
mars_base.source: One-way light delay about 3-22 min depending on the positions of the planets (20 min used for the demo). Surface dose rate 0.67 mSv/day: RAD instrument on the Curiosity rover, Aug 2012-Jun 2013, near solar maximum (Hassler et al., Science 2014). Resupply window ~26 months (assumption).

mars_transit.label: Earth-Mars transit
mars_transit.source: Dose rate 1.8 mSv/day: RAD instrument during Curiosity's cruise to Mars (Zeitlin et al., Science 2013). Delay grows over the transit; fixed at a representative mid-transit value for the demo (assumption). No resupply in transit.

moon_base.label: Moon base
moon_base.source: ~1.3 s one-way light delay. Dose rate 1.369 mSv/day: LND instrument on the Chang'e-4 lander (Zhang et al., Science Advances 2020) - a CNSA mission, not a NASA measurement. Resupply ~6 months (assumption).

iss.label: ISS
iss.source: ~0 delay. Dose rate 0.523 mSv/day: no primary source found, treated as an assumption. Resupply 2-3 months (assumption, midpoint used).

assumptions.next_resupply_in_days: Demo assumption, not a NASA value: days until the next scheduled cargo for each context (Mars 380, Moon 120, ISS 45, transit none). Chosen so the seeded ~412-day stock covers the Mars window with a small margin.
assumptions.solar_storm_dose_msv: Assumption: a solar particle event adds a one-off dose, configurable 10-500 mSv (default 50 mSv, the order of magnitude of a sheltered crew in a large event).
assumptions.bone_loss_attenuation: Assumption: resistive exercise attenuates in-flight bone loss linearly, up to 50% at >= 2 h/day.
assumptions.kcal_per_kg: Approximation: 7700 kcal of cumulative energy imbalance per kg of body-mass change. A common rule of thumb, not a NASA value.
assumptions.iss_radiation_msv_day: Assumption: 0.523 mSv/day in low Earth orbit. No primary source was found for this exact figure; it is an order of magnitude only.

notes: Every value here is either a sourced reference (see "sources") or an explicitly flagged assumption (see "assumptions"). None is a measured constant for this fictional crew. Rules chosen for the demo live in demo_rules.json, not here.

sources.status: Checked on 14 Nov 2026 from press releases, agency pages and abstracts, not from the full text of the papers. Links and reading notes: docs/nasa-resources.md.
sources.five_hazards: NASA Human Research Program, 5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight (official resource of the challenge)
sources.radiation_career_limit_msv: NASA-STD-3001, career limit of 600 mSv effective dose; NASA OCHMO radiation protection technical brief
sources.mars_surface_dose: Hassler et al., Science 343 (2014), doi:10.1126/science.1244797; SwRI release gives 0.67 mSv/day
sources.mars_transit_dose: Zeitlin et al., Science 340 (2013); 1.8 mSv/day in the SwRI release, 1.84 in other reports
sources.moon_surface_dose: Zhang et al., Science Advances 6 (2020), doi:10.1126/sciadv.aaz1334 - Chang'e-4 (CNSA), not NASA
sources.bone_loss_pct_per_month_in_flight: About 1-1.5 % per month on average, more at the hip. Canadian Space Agency, TBone studies; systematic review in PMC (PMC7200725)
sources.mars_delay: About 3-22 min one way, up to 44 min round trip. NASA, Communication Delays, Disruptions, and Blackouts for Crewed Mars Missions (NTRS 20220013418)
